newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, seen down on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, seen down on Tuesday.

text.p: Polish shares on Friday eased after a two-day rise but analysts said stronger selling after price fixing signalled another fall on Tuesday after Monday's holiday as the market takes a breather after recent gains.
"There should be a fall on Tuesday and then a horizontal or slightly downward trend...after recent buying at a discount," said Krzysztof Rogalski of Bank Staropolski brokerage.
The main market has seen two one-day jumps of over three percent this week and last after a previous 14.6-percent fall.
Analysts said investors would be watching the Senate's vote next week on 1997's tax rates.
Last month parliament's lower house voted to cut taxes for low earners, seen as inflationary move, but the bill can be still rejected by the Senate or vetoed by the president.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.3 percent to 13,874.8 points and turnover fell 16.6 percent to 74.5 million zlotys ($26.5 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 47 to 15 with 18 stocks flat.
Analysts said top mover construction firm Mostostal Zabrze, up 5.5 percent, rebounded after Thursday's surprise 9.9-percent fall.
Mass privatisation NFI units fell 1.4 percent to 140.5 zlotys ($50) in the regular bourse session and fell the same amount in continuous trade to 137 zlotys ($48.8).
